title: Hidden Gems in Brijuni, Croatia: Lesser-Known Spots 2027
metaDescription: Skip the safari train. Find Brijuni's quieter spots: Mali Brijun's Minor Fort, Gradina hill fort, Cape Ploče footprints and St Jerolim swimming, with euro prices.
content:
## Quick Overview: What Counts as Off the Path on Brijuni?

Most visitors arrive on a 15-minute boat ride from Fažana across the 2 km strait, ride the tourist train for about an hour, and leave within four hours. The quieter parts of the park lie outside that loop: a second island, hill-top ruins, shoreline rock and small islets. Brijuni has 14 islands and islets, and only Veliki Brijun is routinely visited.

## Mali Brijun: The Island Most Day-Trippers Skip

Mali Brijun is reached only by speedboat from Fažana on a guided premium tour. The route covers the Minor Fort, an educational trail and the Stone Bridge. The price is €250 per person from 1 June to 30 September and €200 from 1 October to 31 May. Children under 7 go free and ages 7 to 18 pay half. Insurance and VAT are included.

The Minor Fort is an Austrian-era fortress. In July and August it serves as an open-air stage for the Ulysses Theatre, so summer evening performances are a rare reason to be on the islands after the day boats have left. Check the park's current programme and book ahead, because access is by organised transport only.

**Opinion:** This is the best-value way to avoid crowds on Brijuni. It costs several times more than the standard ticket, but it is the only way to see the archipelago without the group-tour pace.

## Gradina Hill Fort: Bronze Age Walls Away From the Train Stops

Gradina is a fortified prehistoric settlement on a small hill near Verige Bay. It keeps its circular walls, an entrance and a necropolis. The train does not climb to it, so visitors on a self-guided ticket reach it on foot or by rented bike. Allow 45 to 60 minutes round trip from the Verige area, and wear closed shoes because the path is stony.

## Dinosaur Tracks Beyond the Dinosaur Park

More than 200 footprints from the Cretaceous period (about 130 to 110 million years ago) are spread across four sites on Veliki Brijun and nearby islets. The best-preserved prints are at Cape Ploče and Cape Vrbanj. The signed Dinosaur Park by the Safari Park is the busy version. The cape shorelines are usually empty. Visit at low sun, because side light makes the three-toed theropod prints much easier to see. Walk only on dry rock, and do not step into the prints.

## Sveti Jerolim: Swimming Without the Main Island Crowds

Sveti Jerolim is a small islet that wooden-boat swim-and-snorkel tours use for a stop of about 150 minutes. Entry to the islet is €7 for adults, paid in cash and charged separately from most boat-tour prices. Bring small notes. Boat tours with lunch start at around €40 to €45, and the glass-bottom boat cruise past Veliki Brijun, Mali Brijun, Kozada and Jerolim is the cheapest way to see the outer islets (from about €20).

## Self-Guided Visit: The Insider Route

The self-guided ticket costs €40 for adults in summer and €30 from October to May. It uses the Brijuni Pocket Guide app with rented bikes or electric cars, and it suits 5 to 8 hours on the island. The guided excursion costs €50 in summer and €35 in winter, and it keeps to the train route. For hidden spots, the self-guided ticket is the better choice.

### Practical Tips

- Take the first boat from Fažana. The coastal paths are quietest before 11:00.
- Bring water and snacks. Food outlets are concentrated around the main harbour area.
- Visit in April, May, late September or October. Prices are lower and the shoreline is quieter.
- Dogs are allowed with a €15 ticket.
- Hotel guests on the island have previously been offered a 15% discount on park entry, so ask when booking.

### Best Time for Each Spot

| Spot | Best time |
|---|---|
| Cape Ploče footprints | Late afternoon, low sun |
| Gradina hill fort | Morning, before the heat |
| Sveti Jerolim | July to September for swimming |
| Minor Fort theatre | July and August evenings |

faq.question: What are the hidden gems in Brijuni?
faq.answer: The least-visited highlights are Mali Brijun with its Minor Fort and Stone Bridge, the Gradina Bronze Age hill fort, the dinosaur tracks at Cape Ploče and Cape Vrbanj, and the swim stop at Sveti Jerolim. All sit outside the standard train route.

faq.question: How much does the Mali Brijun tour cost?
faq.answer: The premium tour costs €250 per person from June to September and €200 from October to May. Children under 7 go free and ages 7 to 18 pay 50%. It includes speedboat transfer from Fažana and a guided visit.

faq.question: Can you see Brijuni without a guided train tour?
faq.answer: Yes. A self-guided ticket costs €40 in summer and €30 from October to May. It works with the Brijuni Pocket Guide app, and bikes or electric cars can be rented on the island.

faq.question: Where can you swim around Brijuni?
faq.answer: Sveti Jerolim is the most popular swim stop, with a €7 cash entry fee for adults. Wooden-boat swim and snorkel tours stop there for about 150 minutes.

quickAnswer: Brijuni's best hidden gems are the Minor Fort and Stone Bridge on Mali Brijun (premium tour from €200), the Bronze Age Gradina hill fort, the dinosaur tracks at Cape Ploče and Cape Vrbanj, and the swim stop at Sveti Jerolim (€7 entry, cash). Self-guided ticket holders reach most of them by bike.
